provisions.summary: Exempts sale of groceries (SNAP-eligible products) from the general excise tax.
provisions.approximation: Groceries are defined as products eligible to be purchased with SNAP benefits. That is close to food for home consumption but not identical: it excludes hot prepared foods, and it includes items such as food-producing seeds and plants. The direction of the error is small and ambiguous.
provisions.quote: "groceries" means products eligible to be purchased with the United States Department of Agriculture's Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits.

provisions.summary: Exempts sale of nonprescription drugs from the general excise tax.
provisions.quote: all of the gross proceeds or gross income received or derived from the sale of nonprescription drugs.

provisions.summary: Replaces the four per cent general excise rate on retailing, contracting, amusements, services and other business with a four-step schedule beginning in taxable year 2026. Every rate in the schedule is blank in the bill text.
provisions.quote: per cent for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025;

provisions.summary: Applies the same four-step schedule, with blank rates, to the tax on leasing real property (other rentals).
provisions.quote: equal to [four]: (1)   per cent for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025;

provisions.summary: Conforms the tourism-related services rate reference to the same four-step schedule, with blank rates.
provisions.quote: subject to a [four per cent] tax rate of: (1)   per cent for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025;

provisions.summary: Deposits the additional general excise revenue from the rate increases into the general fund for taxable years 2025 through 2028.
provisions.quote: the additional revenues generated and collected from the increase in general excise tax rates imposed by sections 3, 4, 5, and 6 of Act

provisions.summary: Excludes unemployment compensation benefits from state income tax.
provisions.quote: (13) Income received as unemployment compensation benefits under chapter 383.

provisions.summary: Removes the advisory that unemployment compensation is subject to state income tax (conforming change).
provisions.quote: Unemployment compensation is subject to federal [and state] income tax;

provisions.summary: Sets standard deductions at the doubled amounts for returns under the AGI thresholds and repeals the scheduled step-ups.
provisions.quote: $4,400 or $8,800 for a return with an adjusted gross income of less than $200,000

provisions.summary: Raises the renters' credit AGI ceiling from $30,000 to $50,000 and the credit per exemption from $50 to $500.
provisions.quote: adjusted gross income of less than [$30,000] $50,000

provisions.summary: Replaces the income tax brackets with a 0% bracket on the first $100,000 of taxable income and 8.25% to 11% above that.
Establishes the Maui recovery special fund in the state treasury.
provisions.quote: There is established in the state treasury the Maui recovery special fund

provisions.summary: Appropriates a blank sum from general revenues into the Maui recovery special fund for FY2025-26 and FY2026-27.
provisions.quote: There is appropriated out of the general revenues of the State of Hawaii the sum of $ or so much thereof as may be necessary

provisions.summary: Appropriates a blank sum from the Maui recovery special fund for wildfire recovery, to be spent by the county of Maui.
provisions.quote: There is appropriated out of the Maui recovery special fund the sum of $ or so much thereof as may be necessary

notes: The bill takes effect upon approval and applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024, so effective is 2025-01-01, a date now in the past. The general excise rate steps (sections 3, 5, 6) leave every percentage blank. The description and purpose clause say the rate reaches six per cent over four years, but the text states no figures. These provisions are therefore flagged blank and left out of the spec; they are also a phase-in by year. The nonprescription drug exemption cannot be expressed in the spec, which allows only groceries, restaurants, apparel and medical_services. The grocery estimate is therefore a partial picture of the bill's general excise effect. Section 4 only conforms a rate reference in the technicians provision and is not listed. Revenue from the rate increase goes to the general fund (section 7), which does not change the estimate. Part VIII (Maui fund, effective July 1, 2025) has blank appropriation amounts.
